labels: Clinical NIHSS, structural CT/MRI and six-month global/upper-limb outcomes. Check availability of each measure and task per participant.
use: Post-stroke neurophysiology and outcome research. The comparison group is healthy, which limits emergency diagnostic evaluation.
terms: Authors offer the study data on reasonable request. Request de-identified recordings linked to clinical outcomes and written terms covering the intended device use. The linked GitHub repository hosts analysis code.

name: MGH E-CAM-S delirium EEG
scope: 373 adults undergoing clinical EEG for altered mental status. Standard 10–20 scalp recordings, at least 20 min. Repository provides 22-by-time MATLAB arrays.
labels: Bedside CAM-S delirium severity and RASS. Thirty-three percent of participants were comatose and were assigned CAM-S 7 by study convention.
use: Restricted noncommercial delirium research only under this route. Assignment of the maximum CAM-S score to coma couples arousal and delirium severity. Check overlap with larger MGH collections.
terms: BDSP Restricted Health Data DUA explicitly excludes commercial product development and validation, including proprietary clinical software and devices.

name: University of Bath prolonged disorders of consciousness and locked-in syndrome
scope: 42 patients (14 unresponsive wakefulness, 17 minimally conscious, 11 locked-in) plus two able-bodied controls. Repeated 16-channel continuous motor-imagery EEG at 250 Hz, stored in MATLAB.
labels: Auditory task triggers, rest and session-linked CRS-R and WHIM behavioural assessments.
use: Compare command-related responses with observed behaviour. Keep repeated sessions grouped per participant and distinguish locked-in syndrome from impaired consciousness.
terms: Controlled access via the research data custodian. Proposed use, relevant ethics evidence and agreement to limits on redistribution and scope are required. Only supplementary materials are public.

name: Lausanne local–global auditory paradigm after cardiac arrest
scope: 28 coma patients on day one, 13 of the same patients repeated on day two, and 15 healthy controls. Eight raw MAT blocks per subject contain 62 scalp EEG channels at 1200 Hz plus EOG/ECG and stimulus triggers.
labels: Auditory local/global regularities, FOUR score by day and favourable/unfavourable outcome.
use: Event-locked auditory processing and arousal after cardiac arrest. Split repeated days by patient. The file schema and licence were verified from NLM's indexed repository metadata. The direct Zenodo file listing was unavailable during this check.
terms: NLM's copy of the Zenodo record lists CC BY-SA 4.0. Preserve provenance and review share-alike obligations for the intended use.

name: WAVEFRONT spreading depolarisations after severe traumatic brain injury
scope: 12 severe TBI patients following decompressive hemicraniectomy. Nineteen 10–20 scalp electrodes were recorded simultaneously with intracranial electrocorticography.
labels: 700 spreading depolarisation events labelled using intracranial recordings.
use: Compare scalp findings against an invasive reference standard. Changes through a surgically opened skull may differ from scalp findings through an intact skull.
terms: The authors may share anonymised raw EEG on request, subject to contractual obligations and data-sharing/cooperative agreements. The openly available software and figure data confer no rights to patient waveforms.

name: Birmingham acute post-traumatic unresponsive states
scope: A UK neurocritical-care study of resting EEG in patients unresponsive after a sedation hold. Twenty-one patients met criteria at EEG, with 18 available for follow-up at three months and 17 at six months. Nineteen scalp electrodes at 256 or 512 Hz.
labels: Contemporaneous GCS, CT grade and Glasgow Outcome Scale–Extended at three and six months.
use: Assess pathological unresponsiveness and recovery after injury. The signal acquisition and OSF deposit are author-reported. The OSF file tree could not be inspected, so original signal availability is pending.
terms: The paper says all data and analysis scripts are deposited on OSF. Contents and reuse licence were not independently verified. Contact the custodian if the archive does not resolve.

name: Hindriks, Rot, van Putten and Tewarie post-arrest 48-hour EEG
scope: Five-minute EDF/EDF+ scalp waveforms recorded around 48 hours after cardiac arrest from patients whose background had become continuous or discontinuous by that time.
labels: Individual EDF filenames mapped to favourable CPC 1–2 or poor CPC 3–5 in source metadata.
use: Selected prognostic comparison with a restricted range of background patterns. Before using for an external test, establish independence from other post-arrest datasets, including I-CARE.
terms: Waveform files are publicly listed with checksums. Exact data-licence text was not independently verified; hold product use pending verification.

name: Pardo-García chronic MCA stroke motor imagery
scope: 18 participants, including eight healthy controls and ten chronic stroke participants. Baseline and post-rehabilitation sessions for patients. BrainVision acquisition with 63 channels at 1000 Hz.
labels: Image-cued hand motor imagery and preparation: pinch versus fist. Group and rehabilitation session.
use: Motor physiology and headband montage-transfer experiments. Longitudinal patient sessions require grouping. The 2026 Zenodo original and NEMAR's BIDS conversion count as one source.
terms: The NEMAR release lists CC BY 4.0.

name: Danish CIED / IFCN sharp-transient validation
scope: 100 patients from two Danish epilepsy centres. The Mendeley release contains 100 annotated EDFs and a diagnostic spreadsheet.
labels: Sharp transients in patients whose habitual events were captured on video-EEG, with epilepsy or nonepileptic event diagnoses. Seven readers assessed selected transients.
use: Test false positives on sharp-looking waveforms. Selected segments cannot establish false alerts per day of continuous monitoring. Mendeley, Dryad and Zenodo describe the same study.
terms: Mendeley waveforms CC BY 4.0. Retain the selected release's attribution and licence.

name: Dhaka EpiEEG-60 v4
scope: 60 people (30 diagnosed with epilepsy and 30 neurologically normal), ages 17–70. Roughly 30 minutes per person at 500 Hz. The archive describes 43 total EEG and auxiliary channels in native Nihon Kohden files.
labels: Neurologist-verified group labels and event-marker files. The source lists clinical events and activation manoeuvres as marker examples.
use: Assess classification and robustness across devices. Inspect individual .EVT files for complete seizure timing before using ictal windows. Only EEG-labelled signals count as scalp EEG.
terms: CC BY 4.0.

name: Mayo Clinic CANTAB scalp EEG in epilepsy
scope: 86 epilepsy-monitoring patients at Mayo Clinic, Rochester. Continuous scalp EEG during five cognitive tasks, obtained with a 31-channel system at 256 Hz.
labels: Task-phase timestamps, standardised cognitive measures, and clinical event or break metadata.
use: Awake cognition and task-context comparison; incidental seizures cannot establish the sensitivity of an event detector.
terms: CC BY 4.0.

name: Nancy simultaneous scalp–SEEG mesial temporal spikes
scope: Seven people with temporal lobe epilepsy, nine mesial temporal networks. Simultaneous acquisition at 512 Hz on a 128-channel system. One-second MATLAB waveform epochs centred on intracranial spikes.
labels: Scalp and intracranial traces aligned to the first deep spike, plus depth-electrode anatomical correspondence.
use: Study which deep interictal discharges reach the scalp and frontal leads. Spike-enriched short segments cannot quantify continuous false alarms.
terms: CC BY 4.0.

name: American University of Beirut EMU epileptic EEG
scope: Six people with epilepsy. Acquired with 21 scalp electrodes at 500 Hz, band-pass and notch filtered with some channels omitted for artefacts.
labels: Published segmentation includes seizure categories and background. Verify event coding and patient linkage in source files.
use: Small independent acquisition and labelled-segment comparison. Source filtering and missing electrodes require checking before montage conversion.
terms: CC BY 4.0.

name: Zurich paediatric scalp high-frequency oscillations (ds003555)
scope: 30 children and adolescents with focal or generalised epilepsy. Sleep scalp EEG and five-minute N3 intervals.
labels: Automated ripple markings in the 80–250 Hz range on selected bipolar N3 intervals.
use: Investigate the dependence of ripple findings on electrodes and acquisition bandwidth. These markings are algorithm-generated, and high-frequency findings require hardware with matching bandwidth.
terms: NEMAR/OpenNeuro lists CC0.

name: Cork neonatal HIE background severity v2
scope: 53 term newborns with hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy. 169 one-hour, multichannel EEGs. EDF and CSV contain alternative encodings.
labels: Two neonatal EEG experts independently graded each hour and reconciled differences into four background severity grades.
use: Evaluate encephalopathic background grading within neonates. Group repeated hours by infant. All enrolled newborns had HIE.
terms: CC BY 4.0 in the dataset README.

name: Kerala routine paediatric interictal discharges
scope: Dataset paper describes 21 children aged 1–17, with routine longitudinal bipolar scalp EDF+ recordings of 23–60 minutes, 18 EEG channels plus ECG, at 256 Hz.
labels: Neurologists identified interictal discharges in 11 children; 10 recordings had no such discharges. Paper describes annotations and derived ten-second epochs.
use: Paediatric spike research. The cited Mendeley release could not be verified as currently downloadable. Confirm access, participant linkage and the data licence with the provider.
terms: Archive access and data licence unconfirmed. The publication's licence does not establish dataset terms.

name: Beijing VEPISET interictal discharges v2
scope: 84 patients, each contributing 20 minutes of continuous raw EEG from Peking Union Medical College Hospital. MATLAB data, release ZIP approximately 16.9 GB.
labels: Five interictal discharge categories by spatial distribution and wake/sleep annotations. Version 2 revised 37 annotations.
use: Evaluate location-specific spike detection and whether restricted electrodes miss particular regions. Interictal labels represent a separate endpoint from seizures.
terms: CC BY 4.0, verified in Figshare release metadata.

name: Blantyre paediatric febrile coma EEG
scope: 290 children admitted with fever and coma, comprising 203 cerebral malaria cases and 87 nonmalarial cases. Thirty-minute 10–20 recordings at 200 Hz within six hours of admission in Blantyre, Malawi.
labels: Clinical and laboratory characterisation of coma aetiology and acute EEG.
use: Possible independent study of EEG findings across causes of coma. Case-control sampling and paediatric setting define the limits of inference.
terms: Authors offer deidentified raw EEG to qualified investigators by request; access terms and product rights require agreement.

name: Shenzhen infantile epileptic spasms EEG
scope: 129 EEG recordings across 10 paediatric patients diagnosed with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome at Shenzhen Children's Hospital.
labels: Clinical and EEG features of infantile epileptic spasms; verify access to time-aligned spasm annotations in any supplied files.
use: Rare paediatric endpoint. Repeated sessions require patient-level grouping; a ten-person cohort cannot establish broad device accuracy.
terms: Hospital-proprietary data. Authors describe access upon reasonable request only.

name: NMT-Events, Rawalpindi annotation extension
scope: 1,075 routine scalp EEGs, comprising 962 normal and 113 abnormal recordings. 21 channels, 200 Hz, EDF, Rawalpindi, Pakistan.
labels: CSV event start, end and channel for sharp/spike patterns and slow waves. Two expert neurologists reviewed the annotations.
use: Test clinically relevant alternatives such as slowing versus spikes. Link to the existing NMT source family and resolve patient/file overlap before splitting or claiming new patients.
terms: CC BY 4.0, explicit on the data record.

name: Zurich simultaneous scalp/depth verbal working memory (ds004752)
scope: 15 epilepsy patients performing a modified Sternberg verbal working-memory task during simultaneous scalp EEG and depth-electrode monitoring.
labels: Trial-by-trial encoding, maintenance, recall and behavioural performance. The source also includes beamformer-reconstructed virtual signals.
use: Study awake task-related patterns and representation across modalities. Keep measured channels separate from reconstructed signals and check overlap with other Zurich cohorts.
terms: NEMAR/OpenNeuro lists CC0.

name: Gaffrey Lab infant microstate reliability (ds004635)
scope: 48 infants aged 5–10 months. Continuous high-density EEG while infants watched calming videos on a caregiver's lap.
labels: Age and controlled viewing context; designed to assess repeatability of microstate measurements.
use: Ancillary infant background/measurement benchmark. The release supplies no anaesthesia or suspected-neuropathology endpoint.
terms: NEMAR/OpenNeuro lists CC0.

name: Paris preterm auditory-evoked delta brushes
scope: 30 EEG files generated in preterm infants at Paris-area neonatal ICUs. The original archive lists individual EDFs and separate derived spectra.
labels: Auditory stimulus timing, preterm age and evoked responses around clicks and other stimuli.
use: Evaluate a physiological developmental pattern that could confound abnormal waveform recognition. Registered study files require access approval.
terms: EDF entries are restricted through Recherche Data Gouv. Confirm permitted use on approval. The separately released analysis code has its own terms.

name: UNIVERSE — native Muse S in the lab and at home
scope: 24 participants. Two archives total 20.3 GB. Muse EEG task recordings span 60.30 hours in controlled sessions and 94.85 hours in uncontrolled settings.
labels: Cognitive tasks, questionnaires and controlled versus real-world settings.
use: Study channel quality and false alerts during ordinary wakefulness. The often-quoted 315 hours includes other device streams.
terms: CC BY 4.0 per dataset metadata indexed by NLM.

name: Muse Sleep-Onset EEG — nm000287
scope: 540 home four-channel Muse recordings from 203 people. TP9, AF7, AF8 and TP10 at 128 Hz as released.
labels: First N2 onset per recording, signal-quality flags and supplied split.
use: Natural sleep onset on the intended electrode locations. A single N2 timestamp provides no complete hypnogram or anaesthesia-response labels.
terms: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Obtain separate rights for commercial use.

name: HEROIC — repeated self-applied Muse 2 recordings
scope: Canadian study enrolled 14 healthy adults for on-site instruction and repeat home recordings. Zenodo v2 lists an 86.2 MB EEG CSV archive and session metadata.
labels: Eyes open, eyes closed and visual oddball events.
use: Measure session variability and recovery of alpha and event-locked signals after self-application. Check released session count against recruitment.
terms: OpenAIRE indexes the dataset as CC BY. Confirm version in the intake record.

name: HERO — Human Experience in Regulated Offices
scope: 24 healthy volunteers, up to two sessions. Level-0 device exports of four-channel Muse EEG with a phase timeline.
labels: Baseline, desk tasks, speaking and thermal conditions.
use: Study speaking and movement as confounders. Repository identifies Muse S and the publication calls it Muse 2. Resolve the hardware before device-specific fitting.
terms: CC BY 4.0 per NLM dataset record.

name: IIT Bombay — mental rotation with four-channel Muse EEG
scope: 38 participants in a multisensor mental-rotation study. EEG includes raw TP9, AF7, AF8 and TP10, with eye tracking and behavioural measurements.
labels: Task difficulty, timing and responses.
use: Awake reference and ocular confounders in an Indian cohort. Stimulus pictures have separate terms.
terms: Authors report CC0 for the Figshare dataset. Verify terms on the selected file version and omit third-party stimuli.

name: Hayes and Magne — Muse 2 semantic-relatedness task
scope: 37 adults. Raw XDF, EEGLAB and BIDS copies of the same four channels and accompanying response stream.
labels: Time-locked word-pair presentations, response times and accuracy.
use: Test alignment and signal reliability. Unconnected fifth AUX contains noise. Count the waveform once across formats.
terms: Public OSF release. Underlying data licence unconfirmed, obtain permission before product use.

name: Tecnológico de Monterrey — Muse 2 cognitive-state data
scope: Four native Muse 2 channels sampled at 256 Hz in engineering students. Tabular files include experimental grouping and temporal markers.
labels: Control versus ASMR exposure and information-processing task phases.
use: Replay low-cost hardware and compare contact/artifact behaviour. Task labels are experiment conditions.
terms: Independent catalogue reports CC BY 4.0 from repository metadata. Reconfirm before incorporation.

name: EESM17 — ear EEG with partial polysomnography
scope: Nine healthy people, home recordings with partial PSG and 14 ear electrodes.
labels: Wake period, sleep and sleep scores.
use: Compare wearable sleep signatures with scalp-reference EEG. Small same-centre sample.
terms: CC0 in release metadata.

name: Surrey cEEGrid — around-ear EEG and polysomnography
scope: 20 healthy volunteers in a UK sleep laboratory. Most have same-night full PSG and around-ear recordings.
labels: Sleep scoring and study session identifiers.
use: Test montage effects on sleep. Original clock alignment was lost and the supplied derivative is a best-effort alignment.
terms: CC0 in release metadata.

name: EESM19 — repeated dry ear EEG and partial PSG
scope: 20 healthy adults recorded at home for four nights each with ear EEG and partial PSG. Ten had twelve extra ear EEG nights each.
labels: Sleep stages on paired nights, diaries and electrode-quality markers.
use: Study repeated contacts and night-to-night variability. Extra nights do not have paired scalp EEG.
terms: CC0 in release metadata.

name: EESM23 — repeated ear EEG during sleep
scope: Ten healthy adults. First two nights per person include PSG. Other nights have ear EEG without PSG. Joint EESM19/23 descriptor reports 320 nights across both studies.
labels: Paired-night sleep reference and pre-sleep video markers.
use: Test partial-montage repeatability. Keep repeated nights together and track shared Aarhus provenance.
terms: CC0 in dataset metadata.

name: Ear-SAAD — simultaneous scalp, around-ear and in-ear EEG
scope: 15 normally hearing participants, about one hour each, 29 scalp EEG plus 3 EOG, 19 around-ear and 12 in-ear channels.
labels: Auditory selective-attention trials and stimuli.
use: Compare signal retained with each electrode configuration using the same underlying events.
terms: CC BY 4.0 per NLM dataset record. Article uses a different licence.

name: Aarhus event-based auditory attention — scalp and in-ear EEG
scope: 24 normally hearing participants with 32 scalp electrodes and six in each ear. 18.4 GB release.
labels: Four auditory attention paradigms, target words, task and trial markers.
use: Compare ear and scalp recovery of time-locked signals in awake participants. Check enrolment overlap with other Aarhus datasets.
terms: Downloadable archive. Dataset-specific reuse licence unconfirmed in reviewed sources.

name: Korea University Mobile BCI — scalp and around-ear EEG with movement
scope: 24 participants with 32 scalp EEG, 14 ear EEG, four EOG channels and IMUs in treadmill conditions.
labels: Oddball and visual evoked tasks at up to four movement speeds.
use: Test movement artefacts against simultaneous scalp and ear channels. Published ERP and SSVEP derivative mirrors share the same cohort.
terms: CC BY 4.0 for data in the original descriptor.

name: Bangladesh ambulatory motion-contaminated EEG
scope: One volunteer with 14-channel EMOTIV EEG and headset motion sensors. MATLAB files converted from the CSV waveform export.
labels: Twelve conditions including eye and head movements, speech and walking.
use: Targeted replay fixture. One recording subject limits generalisation.
terms: CC BY 4.0 on Mendeley Data.

name: PhysioMotion Artifact — manually timed artefacts
scope: 30 healthy participants performing 16 instructed tasks. Continuous scalp waveforms released in BIDS with manual annotation files.
labels: Fourteen physiological artefact types with point-wise timing.
use: Develop and benchmark signal-quality flags. Deliberately induced movement is different from intraoperative electrical interference.
terms: CC0 in dataset metadata.

name: Sustained-attention driving task — original raw release
scope: 27 healthy adults and 62 simulator sessions, 32 EEG channels with vehicle position.
labels: Lane deviations and driver response times.
use: Research vigilance and behavioural latency. Driver responses are a task-specific proxy. Omit preprocessed duplicate release.
terms: CC BY 4.0 in NLM dataset record.

name: San Juan Drivers Drowsiness Database
scope: Ten adults, two trials each, 40 hours total. Four EEG channels, two EOG and one ECG in EDF.
labels: Drowsiness event times in separate annotations.
use: Low-channel natural drowsiness comparator. Same recordings mirrored on Zenodo.
terms: CC0 under Dryad dataset terms.

name: Penn EMU reduced seizure-montage simulation cohort
scope: 436 patients, 466 admissions, 1,683 seizures and 1,527 interictal clips. Original 256 Hz clinical scalp EEG used to simulate reduced montages.
labels: Clinical seizure onset and offset and selected interictal clips.
use: Investigate events missed on reduced montages. Computed montages cannot reproduce headband contact problems. Public Box includes intermediate results only.
terms: Authors state that raw EEG may be requested subject to IRB requirements and a data use agreement.

name: Surrey Dreem EEG in older adults and people with Alzheimer’s disease
scope: 62 older adults including 12 with Alzheimer’s disease in a headband sleep study with PSG assessment.
labels: Overnight staging, spectral comparisons and study groups.
use: Evaluate sleep signatures in older adults with the target headband concept. Confirm paired nights on receipt. Cohort was recruited for device and sleep assessment.
terms: Authors invite reasonable requests. Confirm availability of raw waveform pairs and product-use terms first.

name: Simons Sleep Project — Dreem3 home EEG
scope: Overall study enrolled 102 autistic children and 98 nonautistic siblings aged 10–17. Five-channel Dreem3 frontal/occipital EEG at 250 Hz, exported with device-bandpass filtering.
labels: Device-generated sleep stages and sleep diaries. The 3,600+ total days/nights across devices is not the EEG-night count.
use: Study child headband sleep signal variability. Split by family and confirm number of valid EEG files. Diagnostic group membership is not an acute diagnostic endpoint.
terms: Access for approved researchers through SFARI Base. Verify proposed product-use scope.

name: Dreem Open Datasets — healthy and obstructive-apnoea PSG
scope: 58.1 GB release with PSG time series in H5 across two study groups. The OSA arm includes 55 consensus-scored patients plus one extra file without consensus.
labels: Multiple scorer hypnograms and consensus sleep stages where available.
use: Assess sleep-pattern ambiguity and scorer agreement. Verify packaged channels before any device-specific comparison.
terms: Public download. Dataset-specific reuse terms require confirmation before product use.

name: bigP3BCI — includes a dry/wet electrode comparison in ALS
scope: Multi-study EDF+ database across healthy and ALS participants. Study N includes 8 ALS participants, 16 channels at 256 Hz and two sessions.
labels: Visual P300 speller targets, stimulus and response events, ALS clinical information where available.
use: Compare electrode systems with participants performing the same task. NEMAR Study N is a subset of the original archive.
terms: CC BY 4.0 on PhysioNet.

name: ETH Zürich — paired dry and pre-gelled sleep electrodes
scope: Four home sleep recordings collected to compare dry and pre-gelled electrodes.
labels: Sleep-stage comparisons and sleep microstructure in the descriptor. Check annotation files individually.
use: Bench-test electrode effects on sleep signatures. Small series.
terms: Public dataset release reported by authors. Dataset-specific licence requires confirmation.

name: Cejnek dementia and MCI EEG
scope: MATLAB scalp EEG from 168 people, including 59 with moderate dementia, 7 with mild cognitive impairment and 102 controls.
labels: Participant-level dementia, MCI or control.
use: Independent dementia comparison. The seven MCI cases give limited information about early disease. The deposit does not establish a biomarker-confirmed dementia subtype.
terms: CC BY 4.0.

name: CAUEEG, Chung-Ang University Hospital
scope: Clinical EDF files and recording-event JSON from a Korean hospital. The dataset has been reported as 1,379 recordings from 1,155 patients.
labels: Clinical diagnoses with MCI, dementia and normal groups. Abnormality and dementia benchmarks have patient-disjoint split options.
use: Test performance in an independent memory-clinic cohort. Use the no-overlap benchmark and retain repeat visits under one patient.
terms: Local ethics committee approval and application. The custodian allows academic and research use only. Commercial permission is unestablished.

name: BDSP TMS and resting EEG in biomarker-positive early Alzheimer’s disease
scope: Study of 42 biomarker-positive early AD participants and 40 older controls. The archive describes baseline resting EEG and TMS-evoked recordings, with sham and stimulation conditions.
labels: AD group, controls, cognitive tests and stimulation conditions. The available measurements vary by subcohort.
use: Research comparison against a biomarker-positive group, keeping spontaneous and evoked EEG separate. Check counts in each modality before analysis.
terms: Registration and signed BDSP Restricted Health DUA. This route explicitly prohibits product development, commercial validation and proprietary device/model improvement.

name: Chamanzar interictal migraine EEG
scope: 128-channel EEG from 18 people with interictal migraine and 21 controls during eyes-open rest and steady-state auditory and visual stimulation.
labels: Migraine group and stimulus condition.
use: Neurological comparator for false positives and for responses to stimulation. The recordings were taken between attacks.
terms: CC BY 4.0. The KiltHub deposit and NEMAR version represent the same study.

name: New Mexico Parkinson’s oddball and resting EEG, ds003490
scope: 25 people with Parkinson’s disease and 25 matched controls. Includes resting eyes-open and eyes-closed EEG, auditory oddball and hand accelerometry.
labels: Patient or control status, on/off dopaminergic medication and within-recording task events.
use: Measure the effects of movement and dopaminergic medication. Both patient visits belong to the same person.
terms: CC0 as listed on the archive mirror.

name: MODMA, Lanzhou depression and controls
scope: 128-electrode experiment with 24 depression outpatients and 29 controls. Separate wearable three-electrode experiment with 26 outpatients and 29 controls. Resting EEG and 128-channel event-related data have separate downloads.
labels: Depression group and experimental condition. The record also describes separate audio data.
use: Explore low-channel variation and outpatient comparators. Do not assume paired simultaneous recordings or unique participants across experiments.
terms: UK Data Service lists the EEG ZIPs as openly downloadable. The custodian’s site requests an EULA. Product training rights require confirmation.

name: EEGET-ALS, home EEG with eye tracking
scope: Scalp EEG and eye tracking during spelling-system tasks from six locked-in ALS patients and 170 healthy participants. Patient recordings were repeated at home. Controls were recorded once in the laboratory.
labels: ALS with locked-in state, healthy comparison group, task and eye movements.
use: Study gaze artefacts and responses without limb movement. Setting is confounded with diagnosis and the patient group is very small.
terms: CC0 on the original Figshare release.

name: BNCI 2014-008, P300 spelling in ALS
scope: Eight-channel EEG from eight people with ALS performing a visual P300 matrix-spelling task.
labels: Stimulus and target labels during spelling.
use: Study stimulus-linked responses in people with motor disability. There are no diagnostic comparator groups.
terms: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 on the NEMAR release. Exclude from product training without separate rights.

name: Lancaster and Ljubljana Huntington’s disease and control EEG
scope: 69 participants in source files, including 15 symptomatic and 12 presymptomatic patients. Twenty-minute continuous eyes-open EEG, 16 channels at 1 kHz, accompanied by fNIRS, ECG and respiration.
labels: Symptomatic Huntington’s, presymptomatic Huntington’s and age-matched control group membership.
use: Neurological comparator, with simultaneous physiology for artefact testing. Control groups overlap. The 2023 deposit supersedes the 2021 release.
terms: Research directory describes the MATLAB arrays and a custodian contact. A direct data download and dataset-specific commercial reuse terms were not confirmed.

name: BrainLat resting EEG, syn51549340
scope: EEG subset of a 780-participant multimodal Latin American cohort. Ten-minute 128-channel BioSemi eyes-closed recordings. The descriptor reports conversion of BDF to EEGLAB SET, rereferencing, filtering, resampling, ICA and interpolation.
labels: Alzheimer’s disease, behavioural variant frontotemporal dementia, Parkinson’s disease, multiple sclerosis and controls, with clinical and cognitive measures.
use: Multicentre comparison across diagnoses. Check diagnostic group coverage at each EEG site. No original unprocessed BDF files were verified. The multimodal cohort total must not be used as the EEG count.
terms: EEG is distributed through Synapse. Confirm dataset and file-level permissions before product use.

name: Stanford NDMDR myotonic dystrophy type 1 resting EEG
scope: Single-session raw EDF from 29 people with clinically or genetically confirmed DM1. The release also includes filtered FIF, EEG quality summaries and artefact-review files.
labels: DM1, sleepiness, caffeine exposure, medication and clinical measures.
use: Evaluate arousal-related confounders in a rare disease. No healthy comparison group is described.
terms: Registration and signed DUA. The paper documents controlled access. Confirm commercial scope with the custodian.

name: India and Tanzania field EEG (OpenNeuro ds007358)
scope: 2,000 participants in the released subset across two countries. Field recordings collected by trained nonspecialist teams.
labels: Eyes open, eyes closed and task conditions. Demographic and questionnaire metadata vary by recording.
use: Use for population and field-acquisition stress testing. Check metadata completeness and electrode placement per recording. A community sample supplies no independent neurological diagnosis.
terms: CC0 shown for this deposit. The wider field study and its published example files overlap this study family.

name: Cuban Human Brain Mapping Project
scope: 282 healthy adults in the multimodal study cohort, aged 18–68. Havana population sample. High-density EEG, 64–120 channels.
labels: Eyes open and closed, hyperventilation and recovery. Cognitive and demographic variables.
use: Useful for baseline variation and physiological slowing in the controlled hyperventilation protocol. Count usable recordings by modality after access.
terms: Registered LORIS access. CONP lists CC BY-NC-SA. Obtain separate product-use permission.

name: Oslo SRM resting-state EEG (OpenNeuro ds003775)
scope: 111 healthy controls, 64-channel BioSemi. Four minutes of eyes-closed EEG, with repeat measurements in a subset.
labels: Eyes-closed rest, demographics and cognitive measures. Raw and cleaned releases are available.
use: Use for repeatability and normal baseline variation. Group repeat visits and raw/cleaned copies by participant.
terms: CC0 shown for this deposit.

name: Normal sleep and sleep deprivation (OpenNeuro ds004902)
scope: 71 volunteers, two counterbalanced visits. 61 electrodes sampled at 500 Hz.
labels: Normal sleep versus sleep deprivation, resting EEG, sleepiness and mood measurements.
use: Use as a within-person challenge for physiological drowsiness. No drug or intraoperative responsiveness labels.
terms: CC0 shown for this deposit.

name: Helsinki Kids 1K (HK1K)
scope: 1,032 typically developing children, infancy to 16 years, with EEG and ECG around NREM sleep onset. EDF waveforms and age/sex CSV.
labels: Developmental age, sex and sleep-onset recording context. Clinical follow-up confirmed typical development.
use: Use for expected childhood rhythms under light sleep. The archive and article differ on minimum age (six versus two months). Confirm from release metadata before subgroup analysis.
terms: Public files. An explicit data licence was not visible in the inspected landing page. Confirm permissions before product training.

name: First-year infant resting EEG (OpenNeuro ds004577)
scope: 103 infants, 130 resting recordings in the first year of life. Some return up to four times.
labels: Age and repeated resting-state recordings.
use: Use for infant maturational variation. Preserve participant identity across repeat measures and evaluate within the recorded state.
terms: CC0 shown for this deposit.

name: Child Mind MIPDB developing-brain EEG
scope: 126 participants aged 6–44 years. High-density raw EEG from a battery of resting and active tasks, alongside eye tracking.
labels: Task timing and behavioural measures, resting recordings and age.
use: Useful for task responsiveness and paediatric variation. This is a separate release from HBN. Check for participant overlap before combining Child Mind releases.
terms: Public data under CC BY-NC-SA. Product use requires separate permission.

name: Brainclinics TDBRAIN
scope: 1,274 participants aged 5–89, 1,345 resting sessions. Raw 26-channel recordings in BrainVision format.
labels: Eyes open/closed, demographics and psychiatric information. Some diagnostic or treatment outcomes are blinded.
use: Use for lifespan and comorbidity confounds. Check indications and blinded fields before assigning labels. Group repeat sessions by person.
terms: Data CC BY 4.0 plus provider DUA. Every data user must independently receive access. The DUA prohibits sharing source data with unapproved users.

name: UCI EEG Database, alcohol dependence visual-task cohort
scope: 122 people in the full release. Up to 120 one-second visual-stimulus trials per person, 64 scalp electrodes at 256 Hz.
labels: Alcohol dependence and comparison group plus stimulus, match and nonmatch trials. Some files contain errors.
use: Use for a task or comorbidity challenge. The legacy train/test files reuse the same people. Use the full data and split by person. No acute intoxication or anaesthetic endpoint.
terms: CC BY 4.0.

name: Younger and older adults performing cued reaction tasks (OpenNeuro ds003690)
scope: 36 younger and 39 older adults. EEG, ECG and pupillography at rest and during active or passive auditory tasks.
labels: Cues, active simple reaction, go/no-go and passive listening conditions.
use: Useful for age-related responsiveness, sensory processing and motor response. The auditory task does not label drug-induced transitions.
terms: CC0 shown for this deposit.

name: NMT-4K-EEG v1.2 (NMT family extension)

scope: 128-channel EGI EEG and structural MRI cohort. Mirror describes preprocessing in associated analysis.
labels: Resting-state condition.
use: Population variation and 128-channel benchmark. Verify native waveform status in the target files before using for raw-voltage intake.
terms: CC0 in NEMAR mirror.

name: OpenBMI (Lee et al. 2019, Korea)
scope: 54 participants across motor imagery, SSVEP and ERP tasks, with repeat sessions and original EEG files.
labels: Cued BCI tasks and repeated acquisitions.
use: Nonclinical multi-paradigm pretraining or robustness. Link task-specific NEMAR mirrors to this source.
terms: Use GigaDB deposit terms. NEMAR task mirrors overlap with parent release.

name: Cho et al. motor imagery (Korea)
scope: Korean motor-imagery scalp recordings released as separate BIDS data on NEMAR.
labels: Cued motor imagery and source trial markers.
use: Sensory/motor confound and independent hardware evaluation.
terms: Public NEMAR release. Verify version-specific reuse terms.

name: BETA SSVEP (Tsinghua)
scope: 70 participants, 64 scalp channels and 40 visual targets, shared via NEMAR.
labels: Stimulus frequency and cued target.
use: Visual-stimulus robustness and montage testing. Keep apart from pathology tasks.
terms: Verify terms on the selected source and mirror release.

name: M3CV multi-session EEG (China)
scope: NEMAR/EEGDash mirror has 95 subjects and 2,469 recordings. Source project reports a larger original cohort.
labels: Multiple controlled tasks and repeated sessions.
use: Cross-session, age and task robustness. Keep original and mirror in one dataset family.
terms: NEMAR lists CC BY 4.0. Respect restrictions on re-identification.

name: 3M-CPSEED Pinyin EEG (OpenNeuro ds006465)
scope: 20 participants, 80 recordings in EEGDash metadata. OpenNeuro includes raw EEG and separate processed data.
labels: Overt, mouthed/silent-intended and imagined Mandarin Pinyin.
use: Speech, jaw activity and signal contamination controls.
terms: CC0 in the public source.

name: THINGS-EEG v1
scope: 50 adults with EEG during a large visual concept task. Original voltages distributed in BIDS on Figshare.
labels: Timed presentation of 22,248 images across 1,854 concepts.
use: Large event-rich source for nonclinical pretraining and response robustness.
terms: Use the raw Figshare deposit terms. The OSF derivatives contain related data for the same cohort.

name: EEGEyeNet (ETH Zürich)
scope: 356 participants with concurrent high-density scalp EEG and eye tracking. Includes raw data and processed task representations.
labels: Target tracking, gaze and eye movements.
use: Grounded ocular artefact learning and headset QA. Use raw subset for waveform work.
terms: CC BY according to the paper. Confirm terms at file release.

name: Multimodal Phenotyping Dataset of Driving Fatigue (MPD-DF)
scope: 50 participants in a two-hour simulator protocol with raw EEG, ECG, EOG and respiration. The linked raw archive is separate from the processed release.
labels: Physician fatigue annotations and questionnaires. EEG was used in the fatigue annotation process.
use: Fatigue and drowsiness nuisance testing with physiological covariates.
terms: Data paper specifies CC BY 4.0. Use the raw dataset linked in its data availability statement.

name: Time is Brain point-of-care EEG during acute stroke evaluation
scope: Clinical study used point-of-care EEG in acute stroke evaluations. No public voltage archive verified.
labels: Nonconvulsive seizures/status epilepticus during acute stroke evaluation.
use: Potential real-world stroke mimic and seizure-in-stroke pathway evaluation.
terms: Study lead only. Verify sharing and waveform scope with the investigators.

name: Turku verbal-command EEG under three anaesthetics
scope: 30 healthy volunteers received dexmedetomidine, propofol or sevoflurane. Continuous 19-channel EEG was recorded at 256 Hz.
labels: Timed commands, loss and return of response and drug arm. Command intervals limit transition-time resolution.
use: Cross-drug testing of responsiveness and monitor lag.
terms: No public waveform release verified. Establish access and permitted use with the custodian.

name: UN-CONSCIOUS study, serial awakenings and reported conscious experience
scope: High-density EEG during dexmedetomidine, propofol or natural sleep in volunteers. Multiple publications analyse NCT03284307.
labels: Serial awakening reports about the preceding 20 seconds, including disconnected experience and unconsciousness.
use: Test which EEG patterns distinguish reported experience from behavioural unresponsiveness.
terms: No public waveform release verified. Obtain recordings, interview labels and terms together.

name: Infant sevoflurane EEG paired with expired concentration
scope: EEG and expired sevoflurane analysed for 61 infants aged up to 3 months. The final analysis included 42 infants.
labels: Expired sevoflurane concentration in matched epochs, including suppression measurements.
use: Infant-specific pharmacodynamic modelling. Concentration is an exposure label. Separate by patient and site before windowing.
terms: Raw EDF acquisition documented. No public raw download or grant of reuse verified.

name: Bogotá burn ICU music therapy, OpenNeuro ds004840
scope: EEG, ECG and EMG from nine participants in an 82-participant trial in adult burn intensive care.
labels: Music intervention and synchronised physiological channels. Check per-participant metadata for medication and recording conditions.
use: ICU signal quality, muscle contamination and multimodal synchronisation. No verified command-response depth target.
terms: CC0 in the index. Retain deposit citation and release metadata.

name: Parkinson’s EEG mortality cohort, OpenNeuro ds007020
scope: 94 resting eyes-open EEG records from people with Parkinson’s disease and age-matched controls.
labels: Parkinson’s/control group and subsequent vital status.
use: Study resting EEG and mortality associations. Review follow-up duration, age, baseline severity and treatment before analysis.
terms: CC0 in the repository index. Verify the download version.

name: Utrecht RESPect intraoperative and long-term epilepsy registry samples
scope: Related OpenNeuro deposits ds003844 and ds003848. Six intraoperative ECoG cases and six long-term ECoG or SEEG cases.
labels: Operative stage or monitoring day and recording state. Check each run for clinical annotations.
use: Compare perioperative and longer intracranial recordings. Keep both releases linked to the registry.
terms: CC0 in the repository index. Audit each archive and electrode modality.

name: BrainQuake, Tsinghua Yuquan Hospital
scope: Ictal and interictal stereo-EEG examples from eight epilepsy patients.
labels: Ictal/interictal recording segments.
use: Intracranial seizure pattern research. Use scalp cohorts for headband performance.
terms: NEMAR reports CC BY 4.0. Preserve upstream attribution and verify original terms.

name: DRE-LZSH stereo-EEG for epileptogenic zone localisation
scope: Ictal and interictal SEEG sampled at 2 kHz in 29 drug-resistant epilepsy patients. NEMAR converts the original Zenodo release.
labels: Clinical information, segment state and channel-level epileptogenic zone annotations. Derived measures are also distributed.
use: Test localisation and seizure-associated patterns within intracranial EEG. Group original and converted files.
terms: NEMAR reports CC BY 4.0. Check original Zenodo terms and version before reuse.

name: SenseFOG multimodal Parkinson’s gait recordings
scope: Provider describes 12 patients with bilateral DBS, while the discovery index reports 11. Includes 48-channel scalp EEG, STN local field potentials, EMG and inertial sensors. Verify usable subjects per modality.
labels: Sitting, standing and walking tasks with gait freezing, medication withdrawal and stimulation off.
use: Disentangle scalp motion contamination from movement-related physiology using synchronised sensors.
terms: NEMAR reports CC BY 4.0. Check per-release metadata and participant coverage.

name: Atieh Schizophrenia EEG (ASEEG), Iran
scope: 198 resting recordings from 101 subjects, 51 with DSM-5 schizophrenia and 50 matched controls. 19 scalp channels at 500 Hz. Zenodo lists EO.rar and EC.rar.
labels: Diagnosis, eyes-open/eyes-closed condition and participant metadata.
use: Independent site for studying resting EEG associations. Resolve medication, matching and preprocessing before pooling.
terms: Zenodo lists downloadable archives. Confirm the specific reuse licence before admitting to a training pool.

name: Fribourg Ultimatum Game in Schizophrenia, ds004000
scope: 128-electrode task EEG in 19 patients with psychosis and 24 controls.
labels: Patient/control group and decision task conditions, with participants in proposer and responder roles.
use: Test whether group differences persist across task roles. Clinical ascertainment is described in the study metadata.
terms: CC0 in the repository index. Verify selected release.

name: Wearanize+ OA, Netherlands
scope: 130 healthy young adults studied for one night each with a Zmax EEG headband and simultaneous PSG, plus wrist and leg sensors. OA is a subset of the same Wearanize+ study.
labels: Sleep stages scored by two human scorers and by USleep. The open release omits questionnaires.
use: Direct paired-sensor test of frontal headband performance and cross-device sleep scoring.
terms: The host limits both versions to scientific research, and prohibits identification. Resolve product rights separately.

name: DANDI 000019, UCSF human speech ECoG
scope: 256-channel implanted electrocorticography in four epilepsy patients during prompted speech. NWB archive with a versioned release.
labels: Spoken consonant-vowel syllables and task timing.
use: Intracranial speech physiology and task-related controls. Epilepsy is the recruitment context, not a seizure label.
terms: DANDI version 0.220126.2148 lists CC BY 4.0.

name: Nanchang visual identity EEG (身份识别脑电数据集)
scope: Five people viewed checkerboard reversals with varied frequency, size, brightness and colour. Provider lists a 767 MB CNT collection.
labels: Visual stimulation parameters and repeated recording blocks.
use: Controlled visual responses and within-person repeatability. Split all blocks of one person together.
terms: Laboratory offers an application/download route. Training and commercial rights unverified.

name: PhysioNet EEG During Mental Arithmetic Tasks, EEGMAT
scope: NEMAR nm000109 reports 36 participants and 72 records. The original deposit distributes short EEG segments cleaned by independent component analysis.
labels: Rest, mental arithmetic and participant performance metadata.
use: Cognitive task controls. Preserve the original cleaning and filtering history.
terms: PhysioNet release licence applies. The NEMAR BIDS copy represents the same subjects.

name: Bern SWEC and ETH Zurich long-term intracranial EEG
scope: NEMAR v1.2.1 reports 50 people, approximately 6,672 hours of intracranial EEG and 460 expert-annotated seizures. Source preprocessing includes filtering and re-referencing.
labels: Electrographic seizure onset and offset, channel and recording metadata.
use: Long-duration intracranial seizure benchmarking. Original and subsequent BIDS versions share data. Evaluate reduced scalp performance separately.
terms: ETH describes research and education use, while NEMAR lists CDLA-Permissive-2.0. Resolve original and mirror rights before product use.

name: China eldBETA visual evoked EEG in older adults
scope: 64-channel recordings from 100 older volunteers. Seven blocks of a nine-target visual stimulation task per participant in the original study.
labels: Target and stimulation timing, repeated blocks and participant age.
use: Age-stratified visual-response and montage testing. Dementia diagnoses are not established by this task.
terms: NEMAR lists CC BY 4.0. Cite the original release and version.

name: Blantyre Malaria Project Epilepsy Study admission EEGs, Malawi
scope: The investigators accessed admission EEG from 70 children with cerebral malaria in the prospective Blantyre cohort. Modified 10–20 scalp recordings were collected during acute illness.
labels: Acute coma, admission EEG and follow-up epilepsy outcome in the analysis subset.
use: Investigate associations with coma and later epilepsy. Check outcome completeness and follow-up for each patient.
terms: The paper documents permission for a secondary analysis. No public waveform release or product use rights verified.
